label: early original-phase step (t=1-2) after w/k/l
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at steps t=1-3. t=2 holds 64% of activation mass, t=1 28%, t=3 8%. It never fires at t=0 or t>=5, and essentially never in the delimiter or copy phases (about 1% of mass). Within that window, how often and how strongly it fires depends on which tokens came before. A preceding w is the strongest driver (prev_tok w gives 9.5x lift), then k (6.3x) and l (4.4x), with weaker effects from p, r, a and d. The current input w/k/d also adds a little. The largest activations come from w/k/l followed by w w (e.g. k w w, l w w, w w w). It fires more on first occurrences of the input token and in sequences with fewer digits. The predicate "t in {1,2} and some w/k/l already seen" catches about 74% of the mass but has low precision (about 0.27): most early steps after w/k/l do not cross the threshold. So the unit looks like a graded, token-weighted sum over the first two or three inputs rather than a clean boolean condition.
